gate_reference: MDB.10: bounded warm queries p95 < 50 ms and p99 < 100 ms under eight closed-loop readers and a writer targeting two writes per second
boundary: in-process vault HTTP route handlers (vulcan_app::serve::route_request_with_sessions): per-request permission-profile resolution, authorization, execution, and JSON response construction; excludes HTTP transport
build: cargo +1.88.0 test --release -p vulcan-app --test note_session_benchmark -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 at commit 3f28dc87 (binary sha256 2ecc6e623e02ce487a942150c6e6708d4d15b0aec45637f271bf929a46adbd75)
requests: six parameter-varied questions (task/project/contact x active/done) per frontend: DQL `TABLE title, status, priority FROM "public/<type>" WHERE status = "<status>" SORT title ASC LIMIT 50`; QueryAst DSL `from notes where type = <type> and status = <status> order by title limit 50`; a Bases view filtering type and status, sorted by title, limit 50; `/notes?where=type = <type>&limit=50`; and the canonical mdbase query for the type and status ordered by title, limit 50. Each reader cycles all requests from a different offset; each reader's first request is excluded; every response is checked against the ordered paths the direct path returned before the run. mdbase is excluded from mixed runs: the writer edits a record body outside mdbase's managed write path, which would measure mdbase's disk-reconciled fallback.
writes: one writer thread, paced to at most two writes per second: a body-only edit of public/contact/01/record-000001.md and an incremental note scan of that path inside one exclusive write section (a note write followed by the daemon watcher's refresh), alternately restoring the record; the edits change no answer
host_conditions: shared development host (8 cores) with browser and agent sessions; load averages per run below; not the designated reference machine
findings: No request waited for a writer or fell back to the direct path (snapshots_unavailable 0): each request reads one read transaction, and every write section commits what note queries observe in one transaction with the store clock.
With two writes per second, readers measured p50 23-27 ms, p95 52-59 ms, and p99 66-80 ms across both scopes: p99 is under the 100 ms target, p95 is above the 50 ms target on this host.

Without writes the same eight readers measured p95 30.5 ms and p99 44 ms. The difference is the writer: each write section (edit, scan, history checkpoint) took about 430 ms of elapsed time and competes with eight closed-loop readers for the same eight cores, and each write invalidates hydrated pages (about 600 re-hydrations per write).
After each write, scopes refresh incrementally (identity_loads stays at the initial one or two per scope).
limitations: development host, not the reference machine
closed-loop readers saturate all cores, so writer CPU directly inflates reader latency
2,000 requests per run, not the 1,000-samples-per-frontend protocol (see note-query-frontends.json for that)
